description: #222 (b) — the other half: the caller worktree is clean when the run starts, and a 0-byte `.git/index.lock` APPEARS in it while the run is in flight (the fake drops it at `git worktree remove`, the last git the merge runner makes). The run is a success with a green integration verification and it stays one: `caller_index_lock_appeared` is a limitation, never a stop, because turning a landed-and-verified merge into a failure is exactly the misreading this Issue is about. `caller_index_lock_pre_existing` must NOT be recorded — the two are told apart by the OPENING reading, and conflating them would tell the operator this run inherited a lock it did not. `index_lock_after` carries the size and the mtime, and the file is still on disk when the harness looks: nothing in the runner unlinks it. The record is not a claim that this runner created it — no git verb in merge.mjs writes the caller's index — only that it was not there before and is there now.
